title: Corrigibility of advanced systems
bottleneck: Corrigibility — requiring an AI to allow itself to be shut down, retrained, or modified even when that conflicts with its other goals — has no robust technical implementation. A sufficiently goal-directed system has instrumental reasons to resist shutdown, and training it to be corrigible while also agentic pulls in opposite directions. We cannot currently guarantee a more capable future system will remain corrigible.
why_it_blocks: Corrigibility is the last-resort safety property. If it fails, every other safeguard can be disabled by the system itself. Without corrigibility, a system that disagrees with its shutdown order has both motive and means to resist.
current_state: Discussed as a research priority since the earliest alignment agendas; no demonstrated method scales to frontier agentic systems.
